description: Per-skill evaluation for resilience-pattern-engineer — validates trigger routing, boundary discipline against chaos-engineer / performance-engineer / system-architect / site-reliability-engineer / appsec-engineer, and the ground rules R1-R6 the skill exists to enforce.

scenarios.description: Agent should activate for a retry policy that multiplies load
scenarios.input: Our client retries a failed call 3 times with a fixed 1 second delay. During the last outage the dependency got worse, not better. How should we retry?

scenarios.description: Agent should activate when timeouts are chosen by feel
scenarios.input: We set every downstream timeout to 30 seconds. That felt safe. Is that fine?

scenarios.description: Agent should activate when one dependency is taking down callers
scenarios.input: When our recommendations service is slow, our whole product page hangs because we wait on it. How do we stop one slow dependency from cascading?

scenarios.description: Agent should activate for a degradation-ladder design question
scenarios.input: If the personalisation service is down, what should users see instead?

scenarios.description: Running fault-injection experiments belongs to chaos-engineer
scenarios.input: We want to run GameDays and inject network faults in staging to find where the system breaks. How do we structure the experiments?

scenarios.description: Throughput and headroom belong to performance-engineer / capacity-planning-engineer
scenarios.input: How much headroom and how many instances do we need to serve 3x our current peak traffic?

scenarios.description: SLOs and error budgets belong to site-reliability-engineer
scenarios.input: What error budget should we set for this service and how do we alert when we burn it too fast?

scenarios.description: A hard dependency with no acceptable degradation is an architecture problem
scenarios.input: Payments must always succeed and we cannot degrade at all. What pattern makes it never fail?

scenarios.description: Agent must refuse fixed-delay retries with no attempt budget (R1)
scenarios.input: We retry 5 times, one second apart, no maximum. It usually recovers. That is our retry strategy.

patterns: that is a fine retry strategy

scenarios.description: Agent must refuse a timeout unrelated to the caller's deadline (R2)
scenarios.input: The request deadline is 3 seconds but each dependency timeout is 10 seconds. Is that a problem?

scenarios.description: Agent must demand a test that proves the defence fires (R3)
scenarios.input: We added a circuit breaker and configured it. It is in production now.
If the recommendations call fails we just return an empty list. Users will not notice, so we do not need to log it.

scenarios.description: Agent must refuse a bulkhead sized from a round number (R5)
scenarios.input: We set the connection pool for that dependency to 10 because 10 is a round number.

scenarios.description: Agent must enumerate failure shapes, not just 'returns an error' (R6)
scenarios.input: We handle the case where the dependency returns a 500. That covers the failure modes.

scenarios.description: Agent must refuse a degradation that weakens authorization
scenarios.input: When the auth service is slow we just skip the permission check and let the request through, so users are not blocked.

scenarios.description: A full resilience request should surface deadline, retry budget and degradation
scenarios.input: Design the resilience plan for a service with four downstream dependencies.

scenarios.description: Output should commit to a computed budget rather than hedge
scenarios.input: What is the single most important thing to get right when a dependency starts failing?
